Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Demo tenant access controls (who gets access + credential distribution + revocation)

Team —

We need to lock down a simple, repeatable access model for the Standard Demo v1 tenant before we open it up broadly. Goal is “safe-by-default” for live prospect calls, while still being fast for field use.

Proposed approach (please sanity check / poke holes):

1) Who gets access (SSO/RBAC)
- Demo Tenant Admins: limited to SE leadership + demo ops (manage routes, quotas, reset scripts)
- Demo Drivers: SEs who run the live API calls + Console clickpath
- Demo Viewers: AEs + PMM (read-only dashboards + scenario pages)

2) Credential distribution
- No shared usernames/passwords.
- Console access: SSO-only (Okta) + group-based RBAC.
- API access for scripts: per-user API keys with expiration (30 days), generated in Console; stored locally by the user (not in shared docs). We can provide a “create key” step in the pre-demo checklist.
- Break-glass: one service account key stored in 1Password w/ audited access, only for demo incident response.

3) Revocation / offboarding
- Okta group removal = immediate Console access revocation.
- API keys: disable all keys for a user on role removal; rotate break-glass key on use.

4) Guardrails
- Default “Viewer” for AEs (no config changes).
- Rate limit / quota protections remain on even for Drivers.

Can you reply with:
- Security must-haves we’re missing (esp. around logging + key handling)
- Who you believe should be in each group (names or criteria)
- Whether we should allow AEs to create their own API keys, or keep API keys SE-only

Draft access matrix (WIP):
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RW-demo-tenant-access (Demo Tenant Access Matrix v1)

Thanks,
Markus
—
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Demo tenant access controls (who gets access + credential distribution + revocation)

This is close. A few security/compliance must-haves for anything that’s used live with prospects:

- SSO enforced for Console (no local auth fallback).
- RBAC: minimum roles should not be “Owner/Admin” except for the smallest possible set.
- API keys:
  - No keys in shared docs/slides (obvious, but worth stating).
  - Prefer short-lived keys (7–14 days) if the product supports it; if not, 30 days is acceptable *only* if revocation is operationally reliable.
  - Key creation should be limited to Drivers/Admins. AEs should not be creating keys.
- Logging:
  - Ensure demo tenant logs don’t capture prompt content by default in any “support bundle” flow.
  - Confirm audit logging is on for role/key changes (who created a key, who changed routes, etc.).
- Revocation SLA:
  - Group removal should be effective immediately.
  - Document operational ownership: who is on the hook during business hours to remove access / revoke keys.

Also suggest adding a “no customer data in demo tenant” banner + acknowledgement in the setup runbook.

Naomi

+1 to Naomi’s notes.

Two additions:

1) Break-glass account
- Treat it as a “service account” with a hard policy:
  - Only SRE + SE Dir can access
  - Access requires ticket/comment in #demo-tenant-ops with reason
  - Rotate immediately after use
- Attach a 1-page procedure to the runbook (so nobody improvises on a live call).

2) Okta groups
- Keep it simple and auditable:
  - okta-group: demo-tenant-admin
  - okta-group: demo-tenant-driver
  - okta-group: demo-tenant-viewer
- Make “viewer” the default, and require approval for “driver/admin”.

Marcus
Product Security

Operationally, we should optimize for:
- “Remove from Okta group” as the single source of truth
- A documented oncall path when access breaks (INT-771 was basically this)

Concrete proposal:
- Tie demo tenant RBAC strictly to Okta groups (no manual role grants in the tenant UI).
- Nightly job to reconcile: any user not in an allowed group gets roles stripped + API keys disabled.
- Break-glass key stored in 1Password vault “Demo Tenant - Restricted” with access limited to:
  - Rafael Mendes
  - Sean Gallagher
  - Markus Klein

Also: if we can’t do short-lived API keys in product yet, we can at least standardize rotation cadence:
- Drivers: rotate monthly
- Break-glass: rotate immediately on use, otherwise quarterly

Happy to own the break-glass procedure doc + the “reconcile job” runbook section.

Rafael
SRE / Demo Ops

Thanks all — capturing decisions + next steps below.

DECISIONS (effective for Standard Demo v1 tenant: rw-demo-std-v1)

A) Roles / who gets what
- demo-tenant-viewer (default): AEs, PMM, Marketing stakeholders
  - Read-only dashboards: latency, token cost, errors, traces
  - Read-only routes/rollouts pages
  - No API key creation
- demo-tenant-driver: SEs running live calls + Console clickpath
  - Can create/disable their own API keys
  - Can run reset scripts (limited)
  - Cannot change global tenant settings
- demo-tenant-admin: small set (SE Dir + Demo Ops + Product Security as needed)
  - Can edit routes/fallback rules, quotas, and scenario configs

Approvals:
- Driver: approved by Markus Klein (or delegate: Simran Kaur when I’m OOO)
- Admin: Markus + Rafael + Marcus Lin (2/3)

B) Credential distribution
- Console: SSO/Okta only. No shared creds.
- API keys:
  - Drivers only
  - Expiration: 30 days for now
  - Storage: local only (password manager recommended); never in shared docs

C) Revocation / offboarding
- Okta group removal = immediate access revocation.
- Nightly reconcile job (Rafael) will strip roles + disable keys for any user not in allowed groups.
- Break-glass:
  - Stored in 1Password vault “Demo Tenant - Restricted”
  - Access limited to Rafael / Sean / Markus
  - Rotate immediately after use

D) Logging / data handling
- Confirmed: no customer/prospect data in demo tenant; we’ll add explicit language to the runbook + pre-demo checklist.
- Audit logs required for: role changes + API key creation/disable.

NEXT STEPS
1) Rafael: publish break-glass procedure + reconcile job notes in Confluence (link in thread).
2) Naomi + Marcus: quick pass on the final text for “demo tenant safety posture” (2-3 bullets) to include in the Security FAQ + deck appendix.
3) Talia: update enablement checklist to include “create/verify Driver API key” and “viewer access request process”.
4) Markus: send out the access request form + initial group population list to Sales/SE leadership.

Attachment stubs:
- Demo Tenant Break-Glass Procedure v0.3 (PDF)
- Demo Tenant Access Matrix v1 (Google Sheet)

Markus
